name: Eliakim
overview: Eliakim was a male king of Judah and the son of Josiah, as recorded in 2 Kings 23:34. His reign is marked by doing evil in the sight of the LORD, indicating a failure to follow God's commands faithfully. This brief profile highlights him primarily as a royal figure with a negative spiritual record.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliakim means 'G-d establishes,' reflecting a theologically significant Hebrew meaning. He was also known as Jehoiakim, which means 'YHWH lifts up, establishes,' emphasizing divine sovereignty in his identity. His titles include 'King of Judah' and 'King Jehoiakim,' underscoring his royal authority over the southern kingdom.
familyAndRelationships: Eliakim was the son of Josiah and the father of Jehoiachin, Zedekiah, and Jerahmeel, indicating a lineage of kingship within the house of Judah. Zebidah is also mentioned as his son. These relationships place Eliakim within the Davidic dynasty, central to Judah's royal history.
scriptureSignificance: Eliakim's significance lies in his role as a king of Judah who did evil in the eyes of the LORD, contributing to the spiritual decline of the kingdom. His reign, situated between Josiah and his sons, reflects a period of disobedience that contrasts with the reforms of his father. This negative spiritual legacy contextualizes the challenges faced by Judah leading up to the Babylonian exile.
